subject: Reserved commit term anchoring and preferred start schedule — Fieldtone

Subject: Dedicated capacity proposal + term options and start-window

Rajiv / Team,

Great speaking yesterday — appreciate the clarity on the production timelines. Attached is an updated dedicated-reserved commit proposal that reflects the sizing we discussed and three term options. High level:

- Commitment tiers (GPU-equivalent pool): 4, 8, 16 (you asked about an 8-A100 equivalent). Pricing per month is shown in the attached (Fieldtone_Dedicated_Proposal_v2.pdf).
- Term options: 12 / 24 / 36 months with progressive discounts and amortized onboarding credits.
- Ramp schedule: we propose a soft-start window (60 days) followed by a firm activation date. We can shift the firm start by up to 30 days with a reduced discount for that quarter.
- SLA / throughput guarantees: see summary table; we typically guarantee baseline throughput for pinned pools and offer burst capacity subject to pool headroom.

Action items for you: please confirm (a) preferred term (12/24/36), (b) target firm start date window (Nov/Dec/Jan), and (c) whether quarterly invoicing is acceptable. Once you confirm, we’ll circulate a tracked redline and SLA workbook.

Attachments: Fieldtone_Dedicated_Proposal_v2.pdf (proposal, 1.2MB)

Thanks,

Rajiv — quick reply from the engineering/commercial side.

- Start date: We can target 2026-12-01 but need a signed commitment + initial payment 30 days prior to provisioning to guarantee the slots. If procurement needs longer approval lead time, we can instead lock a 60-day soft-start window that begins on the PO date.

- Discounting: Our standard pricing bands support 12mo (baseline), 24mo (15% off list), 36mo (25% off list). To move to 30% on 36mo we need a firm long-term capacity anchor (minimum pool = 8 A100-equivalent) and a commitment to quarterly invoicing with a non-cancellable provision for the first 6 months. Alternatively, we can offer a stepped discount: 25% upfront for signing and a 3% retroactive bill credit after month 12 contingent on hitting commit usage.

- Throughput / GPU sizing: attaching SLA_Throughput_Table.xlsx — this maps pool sizes to token/sec and tail-latencies for our verified models. For an 8-A100 equivalent pool we guarantee baseline throughput at 120k tokens/min sustained with 95th%-ile latency below 220ms for small-context generation. Burst policy allows up to +30% sustained for short windows; long bursts subject to HWM preemption.

- Ramp schedule suggestion: 0–30 days provision detection & smoke tests, 31–90 days progressive traffic ramp to commit levels, with credits for missed throughput milestones prorated monthly.

If you can confirm firm start preference and appetite for the capacity anchor, I’ll assemble the commercial redline for legal and route to DocuSign.

Best,
Rishi
Director, Capacity Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLA_Throughput_Table.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)]

Thanks, Rishi — that helps. A few counterpoints from our side after reviewing with finance & infra: 

• Discount: procurement will only sign 36 months if we hit 30% — show of faith on their side. Could Redwood do 28% as a compromise?
• Start date: we prefer 2026-12-01 firm start (not soft-start) due to product roadmap. If Redwood needs signed payment earlier we can accelerate approvals but need an invoice cadence that works with our quarter close (quarterly invoicing preferred).
• GPU sizing: 8 A100-equivalent is correct. We will require a written throughput SLO in the MSA with an explicit credit table for misses (e.g., % credit for each 0.1% below 99.5% monthly).

Attaching our procurement timeline and desired sign-off milestones to this thread. Also: are there any onboarding credits or free burst credits you can offer to help our initial month?

—Rajiv
[Attachment: Fieldtone_Procurement_Timeline.pdf (1 page)]

Rajiv — appreciate the candor and the procurement timeline. Proposed compromise below to keep this moving: 

1) Commercial: 36-month reserved commit at 28% off list if Fieldtone commits to the 8-A100-equivalent pool and agrees to quarterly invoicing. The first payment will be due 30 days before provisioning; we can accept a signed PO + internal approval memo as trigger.

2) Start date & ramp: Firm provisioning target 2026-12-01 with a 60-day finalization window (i.e., if provisioning slips we push to 2027-01-30 but keep the 28% rate provided initial PO is received by 2026-11-15). Ramp schedule and milestone credits are detailed in SLA_Throughput_Table.xlsx (attached) — baseline SLO guarantee: 99.25% monthly throughput availability; credit scale: 5% invoiced credit for misses between 99.25–98.0%, 12% credit below 98.0% (gradated monthly). If you require 99.5% baseline we can discuss a premium add-on that reduces credits but increases unit pricing.

3) Onboarding incentives: we can provide a one-time onboarding credit equal to 5% of the first quarter invoiced amount as a bill credit applied month 2 if baseline smoke tests complete within 14 days of provisioning.

Next steps: If this sounds acceptable I’ll have legal prepare a redline (MSA + SOW + SLA workbook) and route to DocuSign. Please confirm by EOD Friday so we can align provisioning and finance.

Best,
Lauren
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
